strengths: Significant scale advancement: 5-10× larger than prior 3D affordance datasets with open-vocabulary annotations (>450 classes, >350 affordances) addressing real limitations of fixed-vocabulary datasets

Well-designed three-stage Affogato-Engine pipeline that systematically addresses identified dataset limitations: annotation mismatch, incomplete coverage, and insufficient resolution through principled multi-view aggregation

Rigorous quality validation with three-tier human evaluation (72.3% 'good'), manual refinement of low-quality instances, and carefully constructed test set with quantified improvements (coverage 0.7532 vs 0.6384, diversity 2.6638 vs 0.6578)

Comprehensive experimental validation demonstrating practical value: smaller cross-dataset generalization gaps (14.3%p vs 66.2%p compared to LASO-trained models), successful open-vocabulary generalization to unseen classes, state-of-the-art on AGD20K with pretraining
First unified 3D-2D affordance grounding dataset with aligned supervision across modalities, enabling new research directions
Clear presentation with well-motivated problem identification and systematic addressing of prior dataset limitations illustrated in Figure 4
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Espresso models are simple combinations of frozen pretrained components (PartField, DINOv2, CLIP); no advances in affordance grounding methods, primarily a 'dataset + validation' contribution

Bounded by foundation models with insufficient root-cause analysis: identified failure modes (irrelevant queries from Gemma3 misclassification, SAM edge bias, occlusion) lack quantitative prevalence estimates; unclear how often these affect the 150K dataset or how errors propagate across stages

Heavy reliance on synthetic data with no real-world validation: all evaluation on renders/curated benchmarks; Table A1 shows significant performance dependency on synthetic background augmentation (1.688→1.571 KLD), raising questions about transfer to real RGB-D/robot observations

Insufficient human annotation comparison: Figure A2 provides only visual comparison; no quantitative metrics correlating Affogato-Engine predictions with human ground truth, making true quality assessment difficult

Generalization claims require qualification: cross-domain testing only within Affogato's four subsets; Table 2 shows LASO→Affogato still has large gaps (OpenAD aIoU: 0.026 vs in-dataset 0.031); true cross-dataset generalization unexplored

Critical design choices lack ablation studies: no justification for 5-view sampling for queries vs 25-view for other stages; no analysis of voting aggregation vs alternatives; missing sensitivity analyses on rendering parameters

Evaluation metric concerns: MAE shows counterintuitive results across datasets (e.g., +48.3%p increases) but paper's response is to 'primarily report' other metrics rather than address root issues or propose alternatives
Insufficient transparency on manual refinement process: barely described; number of refined instances, inter-annotator agreement, and representativeness of 5K test set unclear relative to 150K total

Ambiguous affordance semantics handling: multiple valid regions often exist; Figure A3 failure cases (e.g., 'hold' referring to multiple objects) relegated to appendix; unclear how pipeline resolves inherent ambiguity
Missing key ablations and analyses: no ablation of three-stage pipeline, no per-stage failure mode prevalence analysis, partial view experiments (Appendix C) are brief despite being interesting

strengths: Large-scale dataset (150K objects, 750K pairs) represents substantial advance in scale over prior work (~23K objects)
Comprehensive automated pipeline thoughtfully combines foundation models (Gemma3, Molmo, SAM) with multi-view aggregation to reduce annotation noise
Thorough experimental evaluation across multiple settings: cross-dataset, cross-domain, and zero-shot evaluation on both 3D and 2D benchmarks
Human quality assessment (5K samples) with test set refinement demonstrates concern for data reliability
Well-structured presentation with informative visualizations and detailed appendices; clear motivation for the problem
First unified treatment of 3D and 2D affordance grounding in single dataset framework
weaknesses: Minimal methodological novelty: Espresso model is trivial (frozen encoders + standard transformer decoder with text embeddings), lacks architectural insights or justified design choices

Critical annotation quality concerns: only 3.3% of dataset (5K of 150K objects) human-evaluated; 15.4% 'bad' rate implies ~22.5K problematic annotations; refinement process for bad samples vaguely described; no inter-annotator agreement reported

Substantial unexplained cross-dataset generalization gaps contradict diversity claims: PointRefer drops 59% (0.105→0.043 aIoU) when trained on Affogato and tested on LASO, suggesting fundamental dataset misalignment

Low absolute performance numbers even in-domain (Espresso-3D aIoU=0.136, PointRefer=0.105) raise questions about task difficulty, annotation ambiguity, or insufficient learning signal, but paper does not address this

Overstated generalization and open-vocabulary claims: model still trains on 750K examples; zero-shot 2D comparison unfair (750K training vs. 50 examples for baselines); unseen class example cherry-picked without systematic held-out evaluation

No ablation studies on pipeline components: missing justification for specific choices (Gemma3, Molmo, SAM); no stage-wise error analysis despite known failure modes (LLM hallucinations, SAM edge bias, occlusions)

Entirely synthetic data from 3D asset renderings without real images/scans; random background augmentation is a workaround admitting domain gap; only 4 Objaverse subcategories selected with unclear representativeness
Problematic metric usage: unreliable MAE still included in tables despite acknowledged scale sensitivity; counterintuitive increases (48.3%p) suggest deep annotation inconsistencies

Limited baselines and comparisons: only 2 prior 3D methods; recent work (3D-AffordanceLLM, SeqAfford) mentioned but not comprehensively compared; 2D zero-shot baselines are LLM-based (different task) rather than task-specific
Insufficient pipeline analysis: no ablations, stage-wise quality metrics, or systematic failure mode quantification; multi-view aggregation mechanism vaguely described
Missing dataset validity analysis: no investigation of selection bias, potential biases in generated queries/heatmaps, or systematic quality variations across object categories
Weak engagement with limitations: brief discussion (~1 paragraph), minimal treatment of cross-dataset gaps, low performance, or synthetic nature; missing societal impact discussion

strengths: Significant scale and diversity improvements: 150K instances (5× larger) with 750K query-heatmap pairs across >450 object classes and >350 affordance types, addressing real limitations in prior 3D AffordanceNet datasets

Clear identification and quantitative demonstration of prior dataset limitations (annotation mismatch, incomplete coverage, insufficient resolution) with concrete examples and coverage/diversity metrics
Novel unified 3D+2D affordance grounding framework: first work integrating both modalities with careful geometric consistency through 3D→2D projection
Comprehensive experimental validation including cross-dataset evaluation (LASO/Affogato), open-vocabulary cross-domain experiments, and zero-shot performance on unseen object categories (e.g., fox)
Well-motivated three-stage automated pipeline (Affogato-Engine) using foundation models with robust multi-view voting-based aggregation addressing consistency issues
Rigorous quality assurance: human evaluation of 5K pairs by 10 domain experts with three-tier rating (72.3% good), manual refinement of low-quality examples, and separate validated test set
Excellent presentation: clear figures, comprehensive tables, thorough implementation details, and honest discussion of limitations supporting reproducibility
Publicly released dataset with strong potential community impact for advancing open-vocabulary affordance understanding research
weaknesses: Limited manual verification of dataset: only 5K/750K pairs (0.67%) manually evaluated; remaining 745K depend entirely on automated pipeline with 15.4% not-good rating, raising concerns about annotation quality propagation; no error analysis across pipeline stages

Synthetic data limitations: Objaverse objects lack natural backgrounds requiring synthetic augmentation; domain gap between synthetic affordances and real-world interaction not thoroughly analyzed; unclear real-world applicability

No real-world validation: no evaluation on actual robot manipulation tasks or embodied agent interactions; AGD20K transfer shows lower performance than some baselines; user studies for affordance quality absent

Incomplete ablations: no analysis of Affogato-Engine stage contributions, multi-view aggregation necessity, or how much improvement comes from scale vs. diversity vs. annotation quality; unclear robustness to different foundation models
Metric reliability concerns: MAE exhibits counterintuitive increases in cross-dataset evaluation (e.g., 48.3%p) acknowledged as annotation scale issues but concerning for evaluation robustness

Limited baseline novelty: Espresso models combine existing components (PartField/DINOv2 + standard decoders) with simple architectures; unclear whether architectural innovations could better exploit the dataset properties
Robustness under occlusion underexplored: Affogato-Partial shows significant performance drops; real-world scenarios often involve occlusions but practical robotics applicability limited

Insufficient error analysis: failure mode discussion relegated to appendix; multi-object scene ambiguities (Figure A3) suggest models struggle with real-world complexity; no inter-annotator agreement reported for human evaluation

strengths: Substantial scale and semantic diversity advancement over prior datasets (750K annotations, >450 classes, >350 affordances vs. ~23-37 in prior work)
Fully automated, reproducible annotation pipeline with thoughtful error mitigation (CoT prompting, multi-view voting, smallest-mask selection); 24-hour execution on 8 H100s is practical
Rigorous quality validation via 5K human-verified test split (84.8% success rate) with detailed failure analysis identifying specific bottlenecks

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (LASO, AGD20K, Affogato-750K), models (OpenAD, PointRefer, Espresso, LISA-7B), and settings (zero-shot, supervised, in-domain, cross-domain)

Strong analytical studies including held-out category filtering (Table 5), synthetic-to-real transfer (Open X-Embodiment), ablations on pipeline components (Fig. 8), scale analysis (Table A3), and cross-domain asymmetry analysis (Table A4)
Symmetric Espresso architecture cleanly isolates dataset contribution from model design choices, enabling fair attribution of improvements to pretraining data
Transparent reporting of implementation details, limitations, and failure modes; reproducible methodology across 3D and 2D domains
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: pipeline sequentially chains existing foundation models without novel integration mechanisms; Espresso models use standard components (PartField, DINOv2, CLIP) without architectural innovation; multi-view voting is conventional consensus approach

Annotation quality concerns: 15.2% error rate affects ~113K samples; Molmo pointing failures (34.9% of pipeline errors) and Gemma3 misidentifications (9.2%) indicate component-level limitations; only 5K samples human-verified, remaining 745K quality unvalidated

Synthetic-data limitations: all annotations from clean Objaverse renderings; domain gap evident from background augmentation requirement; synthetic-to-real evaluation limited to single dataset (Open X-Embodiment) without quantitative metrics; camera coverage misses internal parts (e.g., occluded brake pedals)

Modest performance improvements on existing benchmarks: LASO unseen +2.1% aIoU for Espresso-3D, PointRefer degrades on seen split (-0.6%), on Affogato-750K itself best achieves only 13.6 aIoU in-domain

Limited cross-domain generalization: strong asymmetry in transfer (18.2 vs. 4.6 aIoU, Table 3); performance severely hampered by narrow Furniture subset (8.8K objects); within-category diversity not analyzed

Experimental limitations: no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; LASO test sets small; zero-shot 2D comparisons against supervised baselines (unfair in Table 4a); concurrent work (3D-AffordanceLLM, LMAffordance3D) mentioned but not directly compared; inconsistent baseline implementations

Scope constraints: only 4 semantic categories despite diversity claims; no scene-level affordances; cannot capture temporal dynamics or force requirements; does not address manipulation-specific affordances

Reproducibility concerns: depends on Objaverse stability; foundation model behavior subject to updates; computational cost (8 H100s × 24h) limits researcher reproducibility; code and dataset links not visible in submission

strengths: Addresses a real bottleneck in affordance understanding by providing a large-scale open-vocabulary dataset with 750K annotations covering 450+ object classes and 350+ affordances, substantially surpassing prior datasets (max ~23 classes, ~18 affordances)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple benchmarks (LASO, AGD20K), baseline comparisons, systematic ablations (CoT effects, mask-size selection, pretraining scale), and held-out category filtering analysis
Well-documented fully automated pipeline with clear error analysis; 84.8% validation success rate on 5K samples reveals failure mode breakdown
Demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple existing methods (OpenAD, PointRefer, AffordanceNet) and synthetic-to-real transfer to robot manipulation scenes
Thorough supplementary materials and implementation details support reproducibility
weaknesses: Critical quality assurance gap: Only 5K of 750K annotations (0.67%) were human-verified; the remaining 745K depend entirely on automated annotation with extrapolated ~15.2% error rate. Training on 113K+ potentially erroneous annotations weakens claims about dataset quality

Modest and questionable improvements undermined by Table 5 analysis: held-out category filtering reveals that most gains (2.1%→0.6% on LASO unseen) come from overlapping categories rather than 'diverse supervision at scale', contradicting the main narrative about scalability and generalization

Severe cross-domain failure (Table 3): 14× performance gap (18.2 vs 4.6 aIoU) between opposite domain transfer directions even after controlling volume (Table A4) indicates poor generalization and suggests models learn dataset-specific patterns rather than robust affordance concepts

Limited technical novelty: the pipeline simply chains existing foundation models (Gemma3→Molmo→MobileSAM) with standard multi-view voting; Espresso models are basic baselines (encoder+decoder); primary contribution is the dataset itself

Insufficient domain gap analysis: synthetic-to-real evaluation is anecdotal (3-4 examples); background augmentation impact (Table A1) confirms substantial domain gap that is acknowledged but not systematically addressed; no evaluation on real-world affordance benchmarks

Incomplete comparisons: 2D zero-shot comparisons against general models rather than affordance-specific methods trained similarly; no comparison with SeqAfford [73]; limited justification for foundation model choices; inconsistent architectures (Espresso-3D finetunes, Espresso-2D freezes encoders) undermines claimed symmetry

Missing critical analyses: no investigation of which affordance types/objects benefit most; limited insight into what makes good affordance datasets; failure cases (Figure A3) show persistent struggles with ambiguous affordances; insufficient evidence that larger synthetic data addresses core challenges

Test set concerns: only 5K human-verified test examples are relatively small; held-out category filtering shows test set behaves differently when categories overlap, suggesting potential selection bias; no test set characteristic analysis
Sequential error propagation in pipeline stages not fully addressed; multi-view voting is a band-aid for imperfect Molmo pointing (34.9% error rate) and Gemma3 misidentification (9.2% error rate)

strengths: Significant dataset contribution: Affogato-750K is 5-10× larger than existing affordance datasets (750K annotations over 150K objects) with substantially greater category diversity (>450 objects, >350 affordances vs. ≤304 and ≤73 in prior work), directly addressing a recognized bottleneck in affordance grounding research

Well-designed automated pipeline: Thoughtful orchestration of foundation models (Gemma3, Molmo, MobileSAM) with clever design choices (CoT prompting, smallest-mask selection, multi-view voting aggregation) achieves 84.8% human-validated quality and effectively corrects per-view errors

Rigorous experimental validation: Comprehensive evaluation across both 3D and 2D domains, multiple metrics, zero-shot and supervised settings, with held-out category filtering analysis (Table 5) addressing data leakage concerns and demonstrating consistent pretraining gains across heterogeneous architectures (0.9-4.0%p on LASO unseen)

Clean methodology for isolating dataset contribution: Symmetric Espresso-3D/2D design effectively separates dataset utility from architectural effects, with proper train-eval separation and dedicated 5K human-verified test split providing reliable evaluation

Strong empirical proof of utility: Consistent improvements across OpenAD, PointRefer, and Espresso models; substantial zero-shot performance gap (40.2 vs. 22-30 SIM on AGD20K); synthetic-to-real transfer to robot scenes (Figure 7) despite domain gap

Transparent research practices: Honest failure mode analysis (Figure 4) with detailed breakdown (84.8% success, 15.2% errors), qualitative comparisons, stage-wise ablations on design choices (CoT, mask selection), and honest discussion of limitations

Clear presentation and comprehensive documentation: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations, detailed implementation details (Appendix B), computational requirements specified (8 H100 GPUs, 24 hours), enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Pipeline primarily orchestrates existing foundation models (Gemma3, Molmo, MobileSAM) without introducing new techniques; multi-view voting aggregation is straightforward; Espresso models follow standard transformer decoder architecture; main contribution is dataset assembly and scale rather than methodological innovation

Foundation model dependency risks: Quality bounded by capabilities of specific models; no ablation comparing foundation model choices or demonstrating generalization to alternatives; reproducibility threatened by potential model updates/deprecation; dataset inherits biases from these models without analysis or mitigation

Uncorrected errors in full dataset: While test set achieves 84.8% quality through human curation, the full 750K dataset retains 15.2% errors; Stage 2 (Molmo pointing) accounts for 34.9% of failure modes; impact of these persistent errors on downstream model training not thoroughly analyzed, particularly concerning for large-scale pretraining

Synthetic data and domain gap limitations: Data from isolated Objaverse renderings without natural backgrounds or context; requires random background augmentation (Table A1) for better transfer; evaluation limited to four Objaverse categories; real-world robotic manipulation evaluation absent; cross-domain asymmetry (18.2 vs. 4.6 aIoU, driven by 14× volume difference) suggests composition-dependent learning

Insufficient query diversity analysis: No quantitative metrics for affordance query diversity; VLMs likely generate similar descriptions across objects; constrained format ('Point to the part where...') limits expressiveness; ablation on CoT (Figure 8a) only qualitative; no human evaluation of query semantic coverage or uniqueness

Modest improvement magnitudes and ceiling effects: Pretraining gains often small (0.9-4.0%p LASO unseen, 0.3-1.6 SIM on AGD20K full supervision); in-domain performance on Affogato-750K (13.6 aIoU) shows substantial headroom; 'unseen' splits don't truly test open-vocabulary generalization (categories remain in-distribution); suggests either data quality limits or that affordance grounding remains fundamentally challenging

Missing critical ablations and analyses: No systematic removal of pipeline components to measure individual importance; no comparison with alternative automated annotation strategies; limited analysis of performance vs. dataset size beyond Table A3; no comparison of heatmap vs. point-based or discrete annotation representations

Dataset availability and long-term reproducibility concerns: Appendix A 'Dataset link' is empty—actual availability unclear at review time; pipeline reproducibility threatened by foundation model version dependencies; difficult for future researchers to extend or replicate if models become unavailable

Limited real-world validation: Synthetic-to-real transfer shown only qualitatively on robot scenes (Figure 7); no quantitative evaluation on actual robotic manipulation tasks; no evaluation of how well affordances transfer to human users or diverse populations; claims about embodied AI relevance not fully validated

Fairness and bias not addressed: No analysis of biases inherited from foundation models or Objaverse; no discussion of affordance understanding across diverse user populations or physical abilities; potential harms from propagating errors at 750K scale not discussed
